summary: אָב is father: the man who begets and is honoured (Exo 20:12), then the forefathers to whom a man is gathered at death and to whom Yahweh swore the land (Gen 15:15; Deu 1:8), the founder of a line or a way of life (Gen 4:20; 17:5), the ‘father’s house’ by which Israel was counted and camped (Num 1:2; 2:2), a title for a prophet, priest or protector (2Ki 2:12; Jdg 17:10; Job 29:16), and Yahweh himself, who made and bought his people (Deu 32:6; Mal 2:10). The verb אָבָה is to be willing, to consent, and is almost always said with ‘not’: men and Israel would not hear, and Yahweh would not destroy (Isa 30:9; 2Ki 8:19). אֶבְיוֹן is the needy man, beside the עָנִי, whom the law protects and Yahweh lifts up (Deu 15:11; 1Sa 2:8). Arabic keeps ʾab ‘father’ (root ʾbw) and ʾabā ‘refuse’ (ʾby) apart, so this one spelling covers two older roots; how אֶבְיוֹן and two rare nouns belong to either is not shown.

words.gloss: father; forefather; founder; father’s house; title of honour
words.summary: About 1,200 times, in every part of scripture. Every Semitic language has the word in the same sense.

senses.definition: The man who begets a child, who is to be honoured and feared with the mother, whose word governs his house and its daughters’ vows, and who teaches and disciplines his son.

evidence.note: “A man shall leave אָבִיו and his mother and cleave to his wife”; quoted by Jesus (Mat 19:5) and Paul (Eph 5:31).
כַּבֵּד אֶת־אָבִיךָ וְאֶת־אִמֶּךָ, “honour your father and your mother”; quoted in Mat 15:4.
“Each of you shall fear his mother and אָבִיו.”
“Listen to your father, זֶה יְלָדֶךָ, this one begot you.”
Isaac to Abraham: אָבִי, “my father”; “here I am, my son”.
A girl’s vow made in her father’s house stands or falls by his word.
A rebellious son who will not hear the voice of אָבִיו or his mother.
“Hear, my son, the instruction of אָבִיךָ.”
Yahweh reproves the one he loves, “וּכְאָב, as a father, the son he delights in”.
“As a father has compassion on sons, Yahweh has compassion on those who fear him.”
“My father and my mother have forsaken me, but Yahweh will take me in.”
Fathers shall not be put to death for sons, nor sons for fathers; compare Ezk 18:20.
“Has the rain a father, or who begot the drops of dew?”: father is the one who begets.

senses.definition: Any male ancestor, and in the plural the generations before, especially Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, whose God Yahweh is, to whom he swore the land, and to whom the dead are gathered.

evidence.note: “I am Yahweh, the God of Abraham אָבִיךָ”: Abraham is Jacob’s grandfather.
“Yahweh, the God of אֲבֹתֵיכֶם, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob”.
“I am the God of your father”; quoted in Act 7:32.
The land Yahweh swore לַאֲבֹתֵיכֶם, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give to them and to their seed after them.
Truth to Jacob and kindness to Abraham, “which you swore to our fathers from days of old”.
“You shall go to your fathers in peace; you shall be buried in a good old age.”
“I will lie with my fathers”: carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their burying place.
All that generation were gathered to their fathers, and another generation arose that did not know Yahweh.
David lay down with his fathers and was buried in the city of David.
“I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your graves in peace”: the two said together.
Not like the covenant I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand out of Egypt; quoted in Heb 8:9.
Visiting the iniquity of fathers on sons to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me.
“Jonadab son of Rechab אָבִינוּ commanded us”: an ancestor two centuries back.

senses.definition: The first of a people, a line or a way of life, from whom the rest come.

evidence.note: Jabal “was אֲבִי, the father of, those who dwell in tents and have livestock”.
Jubal, “father of all who handle the lyre and pipe”.
Shem, “father of all the sons of Eber”.
“You shall be לְאַב הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם, father of a multitude of nations.”
Abram renamed Abraham, “for אַב־הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם I have made you”; quoted in Rom 4:17.

senses.definition: The household or clan that descends from one father and bears his name: the unit, under its head, by which Israel was numbered, camped and represented.

evidence.note: “Take the sum of all the congregation … by their families, לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם, by the number of names.”
A man from each tribe, “each the head of his father’s house”.
Each by his standard, with the signs of their fathers’ house, they camp around the tent of meeting.
“A rod for each father’s house (לְבֵית אָב) … twelve rods”: here the house is a whole tribe.
“These are the heads of their fathers’ houses”: the sons of Reuben, the families of Reuben.
רָאשֵׁי הָאָבוֹת, “the heads of the fathers” of the family of Gilead: the house is named by the father alone.
“Go from your land, your kindred and בֵּית אָבִיךָ.”
Jacob “longed for your father’s house”.

senses.gloss: father: title of a prophet, priest, counsellor, protector
senses.definition: One who stands to others as a father does, guiding, counselling, providing for and protecting them; said in respect to a prophet, a priest, a king’s counsellor or a benefactor.

evidence.note: Elisha, as Elijah is taken: “אָבִי אָבִי, the chariot of Israel and its horsemen!”
King Joash weeps over the dying Elisha with the same words.
The king of Israel to Elisha: “Shall I strike them, אָבִי?”
Naaman’s servants address their master: “אָבִי, if the prophet had told you some great thing …”
Micah to the Levite: “be to me לְאָב וּלְכֹהֵן, a father and a priest”; so the Danites in Jdg 18:19.
“God made me לְאָב לְפַרְעֹה, and lord of all his house and ruler over all the land of Egypt.”
“I was a father to the אֶבְיוֹנִים, and the cause of one I did not know I searched out.”
Eliakim, given Shebna’s robe and rule, “shall be a father to the inhabitant of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah”.
David to Saul, his king and father-in-law: “אָבִי, see, the skirt of your robe in my hand.”
The son given, whose name is called … אֲבִי עַד, “father of perpetuity”, with “prince of peace”.
“To the pit I have called, ‘You are my father’”: the grave as his kin, in despair.
“Saying to a tree, ‘You are my father’”: the title given to an idol.

senses.definition: Yahweh as father of Israel, who made, bought and formed them and redeems them, and as father to David’s son, who calls him ‘my father, my God’.

evidence.note: “Is he not אָבִיךָ who bought you? He made you and established you.”
“You are our father, though Abraham does not know us … you, Yahweh, are our father, our redeemer (גֹּאֲלֵנוּ).”
“Yahweh, you are our father; we are the clay and you our potter.”
“Have we not all one father? Has not one God (אֵל) created us?”
“A son honours a father … if I am a father, where is my honour?”
“I said, you shall call me אָבִי, and not turn back from following me.”
“I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.”
“Father of the fatherless and judge of widows is God in his holy dwelling.”
To David’s seed: “I will be to him לְאָב, and he shall be to me לְבֵן”; quoted of Jesus in Heb 1:5.
David’s son “shall call me, אָבִי אָתָּה, my God (אֵלִי) and the rock of my salvation”.
“Blessed are you, Yahweh, God of Israel אָבִינוּ”: God of Israel our father (the patriarch).

evidence.locator: Gen.2.24, אָבִיו → πατέρα; Exo.20.12, אָבִיךָ → πατέρα; 2Sa.7.14, לְאָב → πατέρα

evidence.note: Jesus quotes Gen 2:24: “a man shall leave his πατέρα and mother”.
Quoting Exo 20:12 and 21:17.
Quoting 2Sa 7:14: “I will be to him a πατέρα, and he shall be to me a son.”
Quoting Gen 17:5: “a πατέρα of many nations I have made you”.
Quoting Exo 3:6: “the God of your πατέρων”.
Quoting Jer 31:32: the covenant made with their πατράσιν.
David “fell asleep and was laid with his πατέρας and saw corruption”.

greek.gloss: family, clan, descent from one father

evidence.locator: Num.1.2, לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם → πατριῶν; Exo.6.14, בֵית־אֲבֹתָם → πατριῶν; Num.17.17, לְבֵית אָב → πατριῶν

evidence.note: Joseph “of the house and πατριᾶς of David”: the father’s house.
“The Father, from whom every πατριά in heaven and on earth is named”; the Peshitta has ܐܒܗܘܬܐ.

parallels.note: Mother, paired with father in the law of honour and of cursing.
God, beside father of Yahweh himself.
Potter, former: the father as maker.
Master, lord: honour owed to a father as fear to a master.
Priest: a Levite hired to be “a father and a priest”.

opposites.note: Son, the other side of the relation.

phrases.gloss: lay down with his fathers: died and was buried
was gathered to his fathers: died

words.summary: The man in want, almost always beside עָנִי “afflicted” or דַּל “poor”; 61 times, mostly in the law, the prophets and the Psalms. Ugaritic has the same word. Its tie to the verb “be willing” (one who wants?) is not shown by any use or cognate, so its place in the root rests on its letters.

senses.definition: One who lacks the means to live and is open to oppression: the brother whom the law tells Israel to open its hand to, who must not be denied justice, and whom Yahweh hears, defends and lifts up.

evidence.note: “The אֶבְיוֹן will not cease from the land; so I command you, open your hand to your brother, to your עָנִי and to your אֶבְיוֹן.”
If there is an אֶבְיוֹן among your brothers, “do not harden your heart or shut your hand from your brother, the אֶבְיוֹן”.
“There shall be no אֶבְיוֹן among you, for Yahweh will surely bless you in the land.”
“You shall not turn aside the justice due to your אֶבְיוֹן in his cause.”
The seventh year’s growth is left “that the אֶבְיֹנֵי of your people may eat”.
“Do not oppress a hired man who is עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן.”
They sell the righteous for silver “and the אֶבְיוֹן for a pair of sandals”.
“To buy the poor for silver and the אֶבְיוֹן for a pair of sandals.”
Sodom’s iniquity: pride, fullness of bread and ease, “and she did not strengthen the hand of the עָנִי and the אֶבְיוֹן”.
“He judged the cause of the עָנִי and the אֶבְיוֹן … is not this to know me?”
“Rich and אֶבְיוֹן together”: its opposite is the rich man.
Yahweh “raises the poor from the dust, from the ash heap lifts the אֶבְיוֹן, to seat them with princes”; so Psa 113:7.
The king “delivers the אֶבְיוֹן who cries, and the עָנִי who has no helper”; 72:13 “the souls of the needy he saves”.
“Yahweh hears the אֶבְיוֹנִים.”
“You have been a stronghold to the poor, a stronghold to the אֶבְיוֹן in his distress.”
“The afflicted and the needy seek water and there is none … I Yahweh will answer them.”
David of himself: “I am עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן; the Lord thinks of me.” So Psa 86:1.
The righteous man “has scattered, he has given to the אֶבְיוֹנִים”; quoted in 2Co 9:9.
Purim kept with “gifts to the אֶבְיוֹנִים”.

evidence.locator: Psa.112.9, לָאֶבְיוֹנִים → πένησιν; Psa.40.18, אֶבְיוֹן → πένης

evidence.note: Paul quotes Psa 112:9: “he has scattered, he has given to the πένησιν; his righteousness remains for ever”.

evidence.locator: Deu.15.4, אֶבְיוֹן → ἐνδεής; Deu.15.11, אֶבְיוֹן → ἐνδεὴς

evidence.note: In the ecclesia at Jerusalem “there was not anyone ἐνδεής among them”: the words of Deu 15:4.

parallels.note: Afflicted, poor: the commonest partner, often as the pair עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן.

words.summary: Qal only, 54 times, and all but a few with לֹא or אַל: “he was not willing”, that is, he refused. Positive only in Isa 1:19 and in Job’s question about the wild ox (Job 39:9).

senses.definition: To be willing to do something asked or proposed, with an infinitive; with ‘not’, to refuse to do it.

evidence.note: “Perhaps the woman will not be willing (לֹא־תֹאבֶה) to come after me to this land.”
“If the woman is not willing to come after you, you are clear of this my oath.”
“He refuses (מֵאֵן) to raise up a name for his brother; he is not willing (לֹא אָבָה) to do the levirate duty.”
David would not drink the water from Bethlehem’s well, and poured it out to Yahweh.
The king of Moab would not let Israel pass.
Saul and the people “were not willing to devote them”: the best of the flocks were spared.
“I was not willing to stretch out my hand against Yahweh’s anointed.”
Yahweh strengthened Pharaoh’s heart, “and he was not willing to let them go”.
Sihon would not let Israel pass, for Yahweh hardened his spirit.
“Will the wild ox be willing to serve you?”
The wronged husband “will not accept any ransom, nor be willing, though you multiply gifts”.

senses.gloss: be willing to hear, obey (with לֹא: refuse to hear)
senses.definition: Of Israel toward Yahweh: to be willing to listen to his voice, law and counsel; with ‘not’, the refusal that runs through their history.

evidence.note: “If you are willing (תֹּאבוּ) and hear, you shall eat the good of the land; but if you refuse (תְּמָאֲנוּ) and rebel, you shall be eaten by the sword.”
“If you walk contrary to me וְלֹא תֹאבוּ לִשְׁמֹעַ לִי, and are not willing to hear me.”
“Lying sons, sons not willing to hear the law of Yahweh.”
“In returning and rest you shall be saved, in quietness and trust shall be your strength; וְלֹא אֲבִיתֶם, and you were not willing.”
“They were not willing to walk in his ways, and did not hear his law.”
“The house of Israel will not be willing to hear you, for they are not willing to hear me.”
They rebelled and would not hear, and did not cast away the idols of Egypt.
“My people did not hear my voice, and Israel לֹא־אָבָה לִי, would none of me.”
Wisdom: “you ignored all my counsel and would none of my reproof.”
“They would none of my counsel; they despised all my reproof.”
“You were not willing to go up, and rebelled against the mouth of Yahweh.”
Amnon “was not willing to hear her voice”.

senses.definition: To give way to someone who entices, with לְ of the person; forbidden toward those who draw to sin.

evidence.note: To the one who entices to other gods: “לֹא־תֹאבֶה לוֹ, you shall not yield to him, nor hear him”.
“My son, if sinners entice you, אַל־תֹּבֵא, do not consent.”

senses.definition: Of Yahweh, always with ‘not’: he would not destroy his people, for his covenant’s or David’s sake, would not hear Balaam, and would not pardon Manasseh’s innocent blood.

evidence.note: “Yahweh heard me that time also; לֹא־אָבָה יַהְוֶה הַשְׁחִיתֶךָ, Yahweh was not willing to destroy you.”
“Yahweh was not willing to destroy Judah, for the sake of David his servant.”
“Because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, he was not willing to destroy them.”
“Yahweh your God was not willing to hear Balaam, and turned the curse into a blessing, because Yahweh loved you”; so Jos 24:10.
“Yahweh will not be willing to forgive him”: the one who blesses himself in his heart’s stubbornness.
The innocent blood Manasseh shed, “and Yahweh was not willing to pardon”.

evidence.locator: Isa.1.19, תֹּאבוּ → θέλητε; Deu.10.10, אָבָה → ἠθέλησεν

evidence.note: “How often I wanted to gather your children … and you were not willing (οὐκ ἠθελήσατε)”: the refusal of Isa 30:15 in the verb the Septuagint uses for אָבָה; an echo, not a quotation.

parallels.note: Hear, obey: being willing is being willing to hear.

opposites.note: Refuse: the opposite of being willing, and with לֹא אָבָה said of the same act.

phrases.gloss: he was not willing: he refused

words.summary: The Aramaic of Daniel and Ezra, nine times, in the same senses as the Hebrew: a king’s father (or predecessor) and the forefathers. Its emphatic form אַבָּא came into Greek as ἀββά.

senses.definition: A father, and in the plural the forefathers whose God is praised and whose sin brought the exile.

evidence.note: The vessels “which Nebuchadnezzar אֲבוּהִי, his father, had taken from the temple”.
“In the days of אֲבוּךְ … King Nebuchadnezzar אֲבוּךְ … made him chief of the magicians”.
The exiles “whom the king אַבִי brought from Judah”.
“The Most High God gave Nebuchadnezzar אֲבוּךְ the kingdom.”
“To you, God of אֲבָהָתִי, my fathers, I give thanks and praise.”
“The book of the records of אֲבָהָתָךְ, your fathers”: the king’s predecessors.
“Because אֲבָהָתַנָא, our fathers, provoked the God of heaven, he gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.”
Indeclinable, from Aramaic אַבָּא, emphatic form of אַב (Hebrew אָב), father; always followed by ὁ πατήρ.
In Gethsemane: “Ἀββά, ὁ πατήρ, all things are possible to you; take this cup from me; yet not what I will, but what you will.”
“You received the spirit of sonship, by which we cry, Ἀββά, ὁ πατήρ.”
“God sent the spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Ἀββά, ὁ πατήρ.”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܐܒܐ (ʾabbā), about 400 verses, for πατήρ: a man’s father, the fathers of Israel, and God the Father. In Mrk 14:36, Rom 8:15 and Gal 4:6 it stands for both ἀββά and ὁ πατήρ.

senses.definition: A man’s father; the forefathers to whom the promise was made and with whom the dead lie; and God, whom Jesus and those who have his spirit call Father.

evidence.note: Gen 2:24: a man shall leave לַאבֻוהי and his mother.
אַבָא אָבי: “Abba, my Father”.
קָרֵינַן אַבַא אַבֻון, “we call, Abba, our Father”.
אַבֻון דּבַשמַיָא, “our Father who is in heaven”.
“I ascend to אָבי וַאבֻוכֻון, my Father and your Father, and my God and your God.”
“He who has seen me has seen the Father.”
2Sa 7:14: “I will be to him לַאבָא”.
David “lay down and was added to אַבָהַוהי, his fathers, and saw corruption”.
“The promise that was made to אַבָהָתַן, our fathers.”
Gen 17:5: “I have made you אַבָא of many nations.”
Fathers of our flesh who disciplined us, and the Father of spirits.
“The Father of lights.”

words.summary: Once, among the pictures of old age: “and the אֲבִיּוֹנָה fails (or bursts)”. What it is rests on later use: the Mishnah’s plural אִבְיוֹנוֹת is the caper’s fruit, and the Septuagint has κάππαρις. Its tie to the root is not clear; if it is to the verb, it would be the berry that stirs desire, which fails in age, but no use or cognate shows that.

senses.definition: A plant or fruit whose failing stands, with the almond, the locust and the doors and grinders of Ecc 12:3–5, for the body’s powers failing before death.

evidence.note: “The almond blossoms, the locust drags itself along, וְתָפֵר הָאֲבִיּוֹנָה, for the man goes to his everlasting home and the mourners go about the streets.”

words.summary: Once, in “ships of אֵבֶה”, set beside the eagle swooping on its prey as a picture of speed. Light reed or papyrus boats fit the line; Akkadian apu “reed-bed” is a possible cognate, though its p is not b. Its tie to the root is not clear.

senses.gloss: reed, papyrus (in אֳנִיּוֹת אֵבֶה, reed boats)
senses.definition: The material of light, swift boats, as Job’s days pass by.

evidence.note: “They pass by like אֳנִיּוֹת אֵבֶה, like an eagle swooping on food”: Job’s days, swifter than a runner (9:25).

words.gloss: fatherhood; family named from a father
words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܐܒܗܘܬܐ (ʾabāhūtā), once, for πατριά.

senses.gloss: family, line descended from a father
senses.definition: A family or house that takes its name from its father, as the Hebrew בֵּית אָב.

evidence.note: The Father, “from whom every אַבָהוּתָא in heaven and on earth is named”.

cognates.gloss: fatherhood, status of father; patronage; intercession
cognates.note: The noun of abu: standing as a father to someone is to be his patron and to speak for him, as Job was “a father to the needy” and searched out their cause (Job 29:16).

evidence.note: “father; ancestor”; from Proto-Semitic *ʔabw-.

cognates.gloss: father; ancestor; (verb أَبَوْتُ) I became a father, was a father to him, fed and reared him
cognates.note: Arabic shows a w as the third letter (dual أَبَوَانِ, “father and mother”; أُبُوَّة “fatherhood”), so its root is ʾbw, apart from ʾby “refuse”. The verb’s sense of feeding and rearing an orphan “as the father does his children” matches the Hebrew father as provider and protector.

evidence.note: “father”; from Proto-Semitic *ʔabw-.

cognates.gloss: father; my father; (plural אֲבָהָן) fathers; origin, source
cognates.note: The Targums’ emphatic form, also used for “my father”: the form Mrk 14:36 keeps as ἀββά.

evidence.note: Targ. Gen. XVII, 4; “Freq. אַבָּא … my father”; “Pl. אֲבָהָן, אֲבָהָתָא Targ. Y. Deut. XXIV, 16”.

cognates.gloss: refuse, refrain or hold back of one’s own will; dislike
cognates.note: Final y (aorist يَأْبَى, verbal noun إِبَاء), root ʾby, apart from ʾbw “father”. The Arabic verb says outright what the Hebrew says with לֹא: refusing of one’s own free choice. Both are words of the will, consent and its withholding.

evidence.note: “He refused; or refrained, forbore, abstained, or held back … voluntarily, or of his own free will or choice … he refused assent, or consent, to the thing”.

cognates.note: Onkelos uses it where the Hebrew of Deu 25:7 has לֹא אָבָה.

evidence.note: “to be willing. Targ. O. Deut. XXV, 7; a. fr.”

cognates.note: As in Arabic, the positive verb is the refusal.
The same form as אֶבְיוֹן, which shows the word was at home in the West Semitic of Canaan.

evidence.note: “poor, impoverished”; “Compare Hebrew אֶבְיוֹן”.

cognates.note: Akkadian p where Hebrew has ב, so the match is uncertain; its sense fits reed boats in Job 9:26.

doctrine.statement: Scripture calls Yahweh the father of Israel as the one who bought, made and established them (Deu 32:6), their potter (Isa 64:7) and their redeemer (Isa 63:16), and Malachi sets “one father” beside “one God (אֵל) created us” (Mal 2:10). To David’s seed he promises, “I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son” (2Sa 7:14; 1Ch 17:13), and that son will call him “my father, my God” (Psa 89:27); Hebrews applies the promise to Jesus (Heb 1:5). Jesus prays “Abba, Father” (Mrk 14:36), speaks of “my Father and your Father, my God and your God” (Jhn 20:17), and those who receive the spirit of sonship cry “Abba, Father” too (Rom 8:15; Gal 4:6). Paul: “to us there is one God, the Father” (1Co 8:6). From the verses: the Father is the one God, Yahweh, who brings his people into being and redeems them; the Son is the promised seed of David, begotten by him, who calls the Father his God.

To die is to “go to your fathers” and be buried (Gen 15:15), to “lie with my fathers” in their burying place (Gen 47:30), to “lie down with his fathers” and be buried in the city of David (1Ki 2:10); Josiah is “gathered to your fathers” and in the same breath “gathered to your graves in peace” (2Ki 22:20). Peter says David is dead and buried, his tomb is with us, and he did not ascend into the heavens (Act 2:29, 34); Paul, that David fell asleep, “was laid with his fathers and saw corruption”, while the one God raised saw none (Act 13:36–37). From the verses: going to the fathers is lying in the grave with them, not passing to a life elsewhere; the hope scripture sets against it is resurrection.

Yahweh swore the land to the fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, “to give to them and to their seed after them” (Deu 1:8; Gen 26:3; 28:13), and Micah looks for the truth and kindness “which you swore to our fathers” (Mic 7:20). Stephen says God gave Abraham no inheritance in it, not a foot’s breadth, yet promised to give it to him and his seed (Act 7:5); they died in faith, not having received the promises (Heb 11:13). Paul preaches “the promise made to the fathers”, fulfilled in raising Jesus (Act 13:32–33), is on trial “for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers” (Act 26:6), and says Christ came “to confirm the promises made to the fathers” (Rom 15:8). Abraham, made “father of a multitude of nations” (Gen 17:5), is heir of the world and father of all who believe (Rom 4:13, 16–17). From the verses: the oath to the fathers is still to be kept to them in person, which requires their resurrection, and those in Christ inherit it with them as Abraham’s seed.

note: Root key אבה: the database files אָב (a.ae.ab) under this key with the verb, as BDB’s II אבה. Two older roots in one spelling: Arabic, Ugaritic, Ge’ez and Aramaic keep ʾb(w) “father” and ʾby “want/refuse” apart (Lane files them as ابو and ابى). ה is not one of the merged letters, so no `sounds` are recorded; the split is shown by the cognate sets instead. אֶבְיוֹן: Ugaritic abyn is the only cognate; Coptic ⲉⲃⲓⲏⲛ “a poor, wretched person” (coptic-lexicon C628, CD 53a) is not recorded, since whether it is Egyptian (bjn “bad”) borrowed into Semitic or the Semitic word borrowed into Egyptian is not shown, and Ugaritic has the word early. Akkadian buʾʾû “look for, seek” was not taken as a cognate of the verb. אֲבִיּוֹנָה: the caper identification rests on the Mishnah (Maaserot 4:6, plural אִבְיוֹנוֹת) and the Septuagint’s κάππαρις (macula-lxx Ecc.12.5); no Greek recorded as it is not in the NT. Left out: Mic 1:15 אָבִי (the brief analyses it as בוא); a.aa.ab and xa.aa.ab (cross-references, no tokens); the gentilic אֲבִי הָעֶזְרִי (a.ae.au, Abiezrite) and all the personal names in אֲבִי-/אַב- (a.ae.*), which belong in names/; אֵב “fresh green, shoot” (a.ab.ab, root אבב) and Aramaic אֵב “fruit” (xa.aa.ac, keyed אב), whose cognates (Akkadian inbu, Ugaritic ib, Syriac ʾebbā) point to another root. Peshitta words from SEDRA root 2 (lexeme 2 ܐܒܐ, about 400 verses; lexeme 3 ܐܒܗܘܬܐ, Eph 3:15 only) with verses from the BFBS word list. Not consulted: Fisher/DULAT for Ugaritic ab and abyn, Krahmalkov for Punic ʾb, Leslau and Dillmann for Ge’ez ʾab and ʾabaya, CAD for abu and abbūtu, Payne Smith for Syriac ܐܒܐ. Open: (1) Isa 9:5 אֲבִי עַד is listed under the title sense with a literal gloss; whether “father of perpetuity” or “father of the age” better fits עַד is for review. (2) Mat 23:37 is an echo of Isa 30:15, not a quotation; review whether to keep it.
